subject: mathematics
title: 3D Mensuration Solids — Surface Area, Volume & Net Unfolder
subtitle: Right circular cylinder, hollow cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere, frustum, and combined solids (π = 22/7)
curiosity_hook: When a hemisphere is glued onto a cylinder to make a medicine capsule, why do their volumes add directly while their total surface areas do not?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 3D Blueprint Build (pending human maths teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Visualize and orbit 3D solids (cylinder, hollow cylinder, cone, sphere, hemisphere, frustum, and combined capsule) with slice cutaway and 2D net equivalents.
Compute Curved Surface Area (CSA), Total Surface Area (TSA), slant height l, and Volume using π = 22/7 per Class 10 textbook convention.
Distinguish why joined faces vanish from exposed TSA in combined solids while total volume remains strictly conserved during shape conversion.

concept_outline.heading: Right Circular Cylinder & Hollow Cylinder (7.2.1–7.2.2)
concept_outline.summary: Revolving a rectangle about one side generates a cylinder. Unfolding its curved surface produces a rectangle of width 2πr and height h (CSA = 2πrh; TSA = 2πr(h + r); V = πr²h).
concept_outline.worked_example: Textbook Example 7.1 (p. 271): Drum with r = 14 cm, h = 20 cm → CSA = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × 20 = 1760 cm²; TSA = 2992 cm².

concept_outline.heading: Cone, Sphere, Hemisphere & Frustum (7.2.3–7.2.7, 7.3)
concept_outline.summary: A cone's slant height satisfies l = √(r² + h²) and its volume is exactly 1/3 of a cylinder with the same base and height. Slicing a cone parallel to its base creates a frustum (CSA = π(R + r)l, V = (1/3)πh(R² + Rr + r²)).
concept_outline.worked_example: For a cone with r = 7 cm and h = 24 cm, slant height l = √(49 + 576) = 25 cm, CSA = (22/7) × 7 × 25 = 550 cm², V = 1232 cm³.

concept_outline.heading: Combined Solids & Volume Conservation (7.4–7.5)
concept_outline.summary: In combined solids (like a cylinder + two hemispheres), total volume equals the sum of component volumes, whereas exposed TSA sums ONLY the outer curved surfaces — excluding internal joined circular bases.

key_terms.definition: The lateral curved area of a 3D solid excluding its flat circular top or bottom bases.
Distance along the slanted side of a cone (√(r² + h²)) or frustum (√(h² + (R − r)²)).
The bottom bucket-shaped portion remaining when a right circular cone is sliced parallel to its base.
Melting and recasting a solid from one 3D shape into another preserves total material volume unchanged.

expected_observations: A cone's volume is always exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with identical r and h.
Solid hemisphere TSA is 3πr² (2πr² curved dome + πr² newly exposed flat circular base), not 2πr².
Setting r = 14 cm, h = 20 cm on Cylinder reproduces Textbook Example 7.1: CSA = 1760 cm² and TSA = 2992 cm².

storyboard.expected_response: CSA reads 1760 cm² and TSA reads 2992 cm² (adding two bases of 616 cm² each).

storyboard.learner_action: Select Combined Solid (Cylinder + 2 Hemispheres) and compare its TSA formula with summing separate TSAs.

steps.heading: Cylinder Net (2πrh + 2πr²)
steps.description: Unrolling a cylinder yields a rectangle of width 2πr and height h plus two circular bases.

steps.heading: Cone & Frustum Slant Height
steps.description: Use Pythagoras to compute slant height l before finding CSA = πrl (cone) or π(R + r)l (frustum).
steps.key_takeaway: Cone volume = (1/3)πr²h; Frustum volume = (1/3)πh(R² + Rr + r²).

steps.heading: Hemisphere & Combined Solids
steps.description: A solid hemisphere exposes one flat circle (TSA = 3πr²), whereas joined internal faces in combined solids are NOT part of exposed TSA.
steps.key_takeaway: Always sum only externally visible curved/flat surfaces for combined TSA.

question_bank.prompt: What is the Total Surface Area (TSA) of a solid hemisphere of radius r?
question_bank.hint: Remember to include the newly exposed flat circular base along with the curved dome.

options.label: 2πr²
options.feedback: 2πr² is only the Curved Surface Area (CSA) of the dome.

options.label: 3πr²
options.feedback: Correct! Curved dome (2πr²) + flat circular base (πr²) = 3πr².

options.label: 4πr²
options.feedback: 4πr² is the surface area of a full sphere.

options.label: (2/3)πr³
options.feedback: (2/3)πr³ is the volume of a solid hemisphere, not its surface area.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Slicing a sphere in half gives curved area 2πr² plus one circular cross-section of area πr², totaling 3πr².

question_bank.prompt: A right circular cylinder has base radius r = 14 cm and height h = 20 cm (π = 22/7). What is its Curved Surface Area?

options.label: 2992 cm²
options.feedback: 2992 cm² is the Total Surface Area including both circular bases.

options.label: 12320 cm²
options.feedback: 12320 cm³ is the volume (πr²h), not the curved surface area.

question_bank.prompt: A right circular cone and a cylinder have the same base radius r and height h. What is the ratio of Volume(Cone) : Volume(Cylinder)?

options.feedback: A cone holds less than half of a cylinder with the same base and height.
Correct! V_cone = (1/3)πr²h is exactly one-third of V_cylinder = πr²h.
2 : 3 is the ratio of a sphere/hemisphere inside a circumscribed cylinder.
Re-check the cone volume formula V = (1/3)πr²h.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Because V_cone = (1/3)πr²h and V_cyl = πr²h, their ratio is always 1 : 3.

question_bank.prompt: When a metallic solid sphere is melted and recast into several small identical cones, which quantity remains unchanged?
question_bank.hint: Think about what is conserved when the same amount of metal changes shape.

options.label: Total surface area
options.feedback: Breaking one sphere into many smaller shapes greatly increases total exposed surface area.

options.label: Total volume of metal
options.feedback: Correct! Section 7.5 Conversion of Solids relies on Volume before = Total Volume after.

options.label: Radius
options.feedback: The radius changes completely when recast into cones.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Neglecting wastage, recasting conserves material volume: V_sphere = N × V_cone.

worked_feedback: Always check whether a problem asks for CSA (curved walls only) or TSA (exposed walls + exposed bases).
In TN Class 10 Mensuration, use π = 22/7 unless π = 3.14 is explicitly stated.

flashcards.front: CSA & TSA of a Right Circular Cylinder
Slant height (l) and Volume of a Frustum of a Cone
Why is TSA of a solid hemisphere 3πr² instead of 2πr²?
flashcards.back: Slicing a sphere exposes a flat circular base (πr²) in addition to half the curved shell (2πr²).
Add only the externally visible curved/flat surfaces — never add internal faces glued together.
